transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Honestly, the thing that kind of scared me into coming in is my eating. It’s been really all over the place lately. Like, some days I’ll get through almost the whole day and realize I basically didn’t eat anything, not because I’m trying to or anything, I just forget meals completely. And then other nights it’s the total opposite — I’m up late, after midnight, and I’m tearing through takeout or snacks like I can’t stop myself.

It’s just been weird enough that I started thinking, okay, maybe I should actually talk to somebody, because it doesn’t feel like my normal routine anymore.
When you eat like that after midnight, are you waking up from sleep to do it?

Not really waking up from sleep, no. It’s more like I’m already still up way too late, and then I suddenly realize I barely ate during the day, or I just get this urge to order food or grab whatever snacks are around. Like I’ll go most of the day and completely forget meals, and then after midnight I’m eating takeout or a bunch of random stuff like I can’t slow down. It’s not like I go to bed and then wake up hungry—it’s more that my whole eating schedule is just… messed up.
When those late-night eating episodes happen, do you feel like you can’t stop eating once you’ve started?

Yeah… kind of. Not every single time, but when it happens it feels like once I start, I’m not really making normal decisions about it. Like I’ll order takeout after midnight or start grabbing snacks, and then it’s just this whole stretch where I’m eating whatever’s there, one thing after another. It’s not even like I’m enjoying it that much the whole time — it’s more like I suddenly realize I barely ate all day, and then I’m tearing through food like my body’s trying to catch up or something.

And that’s what freaked me out, honestly, because it’s such a swing from forgetting meals completely during the day to then being up late and eating way more than feels normal. It doesn’t feel like my usual appetite or routine.
Are you worried about gaining weight or about the shape of your body?

I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, I’m not thrilled if my clothes feel tighter or something, like anyone, but I’m not sitting there counting calories because I’m scared of gaining weight, and I’m not avoiding food because of how I think I look.

It’s more like I just genuinely forget to eat or I’m distracted, and then later it catches up with me in this messy way. The late-night eating bothers me because it feels out of control and makes me feel kind of gross afterward, but I wouldn’t say it’s about my body shape exactly. It’s more the pattern that worries me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

Yeah… I guess I have. It’s hard for me to say “depressed” because I keep telling myself I’m just stressed or I’m tired or I’m being dramatic, but if I’m being honest, the low feeling has been there most days for a while now.

It’s probably been around four months, give or take. Like this heavy mood, and feeling guilty about things, and just not really caring about stuff the way I normally would. At first I thought it was just a bad week turning into a bad couple weeks, but it didn’t really lift. And after the trouble I had at work, it got a lot harder to ignore. That’s when it felt less like, “Oh, I’m just in a funk,” and more like, “Okay, something is actually off here.”
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… definitely. That’s actually one of the things that makes me feel like I’m not really myself lately.

I used to be pretty into my weekends, like I’d play soccer with some guys, and even if I was tired from the week I’d usually still want to go because once I got there it felt good, you know? Now I’ll see the messages about it and just… ignore them, or tell myself I’ll answer later, and then I don’t. It’s not even that I hate it now, it’s more like I can’t make myself care enough to show up.

Same with cooking. I used to like making dinner for my girlfriend — not fancy chef stuff or anything, but I liked planning something, going to the store, making it feel like a nice night. Lately it feels like this huge task, and the fun part of it is just gone.

Even stuff like checking out small galleries, which used to be something I’d do just because it got me out of my head, I haven’t cared about. And at work, I used to actually enjoy helping the newer sales guys figure things out, like giving them tips or walking them through how to handle certain accounts. Now when they ask me something, I feel bad because I know I should care, but I just don’t have that spark for it. It all feels kind of flat.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?

Yeah, I have. It’s like… even if I technically lie down for a long time, it doesn’t feel like I really get my energy back. I’ll spend hours resting, and then the next day my body still feels drained.

And it’s not just “I don’t feel like doing stuff.” It’s physical, too. Like at work, carrying sample cases into a client meeting will feel way harder than it should. I’ll be thinking, “Why am I this worn out from something I normally just do without thinking?” It’s embarrassing, honestly, because it makes me feel kind of weak or like I’m dragging myself through things that used to be normal.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Yeah… my sleep’s been pretty messed up. Most nights it’s one of two things. Either I get in bed and I’m exhausted, like I feel tired, but then my brain just won’t shut off. I’ll start running through work stuff — pitches, what I should’ve said to a client, what I need to say next time, different ways to phrase things — and it just keeps looping. It’s like I’m rehearsing conversations I’m not even having yet.

Or I’ll fall asleep for a bit, but then I wake up way before my alarm, like way too early, and I’m just… awake. Not rested, though. It’s weird because I know I barely slept, and part of me is like, “You need to go back to sleep,” but my body feels kind of wired, like I’m already switched on. So then I just lie there, thinking about the day before it’s even started. It’s been happening a lot, most nights honestly.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of killing yourself?

Yeah… I mean, not like I’ve sat down and made some plan or anything like that. I haven’t done that. But I’d be lying if I said the thoughts weren’t there sometimes.

It’s more like… I’ll be so tired of feeling like this that I’ll think, “I wish I could just not wake up for a while.” Not even necessarily die, exactly, but just stop having to be conscious and deal with everything for a bit. Like if I could press pause on myself and not have to feel anything, that sounds… honestly kind of relieving sometimes.

But no, I haven’t planned to hurt myself. I haven’t picked a way or anything. It’s more those thoughts of not wanting to be here in the moment, or wanting everything to just go quiet.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?

Yeah, definitely. That’s actually been one of the more frustrating things, because my job is a lot of little details, and normally I’m pretty good at keeping track of them.

Like I’ll be entering an order, and I know what I’m supposed to be doing — customer name, quantities, item numbers, shipping details, all that basic stuff — but then my phone buzzes, or a truck goes by outside, or someone just walks past the office, and it completely pulls me off. Not just for a second, either. It’s like my attention gets yanked over there, and then when I look back at the screen I’ve lost the thread of what I was doing.

And then I’ll miss things I normally wouldn’t miss. Basic details. Stuff where afterward I’m like, “How did I not catch that?” It makes me feel kind of stupid, honestly, because these aren’t complicated tasks for me. I’ve done them a million times. But lately it feels like my brain is way too easy to knock off track.
Have you had less appetite lately?

Yeah… kind of, but it’s not just less appetite exactly. It’s been really uneven, and honestly that’s part of what scared me into coming in.

Some days I’ll realize it’s like mid-afternoon and I haven’t eaten anything real at all. Not because I’m trying not to eat, I just… forget, or nothing sounds good, or I’m busy and then suddenly hours are gone. And then other nights it swings the other way where it’s after midnight and I’m tearing through takeout or snacks like I’m starving, just eating whatever’s there.

So I don’t know if I’d call it just “less appetite,” because sometimes it’s like I have no appetite, and then later it’s like I’m making up for the whole day all at once. It feels out of control in a weird way.
Lately, have other people noticed that you’re moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

I don’t know if people would say “slower,” exactly. I haven’t had someone sit me down and say, like, “You’re moving slow” or anything.

It’s more like I feel kind of all over the place depending on where I am. At work, before appointments, I’ll catch myself pacing around my car in the parking lot instead of just going in. Like I’ll get there early, and instead of sitting still I’m walking around the car, checking my phone, tapping my hands on the steering wheel, almost like I can’t settle my body down. I probably look ridiculous if anyone sees me.

But then when I get home, it’s the opposite. I’ll sit on the couch and it feels like getting up to do one basic thing takes forever. Like I know I should stand up, or go get something, or move to the next room, but my body feels heavy and I just sit there thinking about doing it. So I don’t know if it’s that I’m moving slower all the time, but there are definitely times where I feel slowed down, and other times where I’m kind of restless and can’t stop moving.
Have you been worrying a lot about different things in a way that feels hard to control?

I’m not really sure how to answer that one. I mean, I worry about things, obviously — work stuff, money stuff, whether I’m messing things up — but I don’t know if it’s “a lot” in the way you mean.

It doesn’t feel like I’m sitting there with one worry after another all day that I can’t control, exactly. Sometimes my mind gets stuck on something for a while, but I can usually tell what it’s connected to. Like if something is actually going on, I’ll think about it too much maybe, but I don’t know if I’d call it this constant uncontrollable worrying about everything.

So… I guess I haven’t really noticed that as the main thing. I’d probably need you to explain what you mean a little more.
During those late-night episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food for the situation?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. Not every time, but on those nights it feels like a weird amount for that hour, if that makes sense.

Like I’ll have barely eaten during the day — maybe I forgot lunch completely or just had something small — and then after midnight I’m suddenly ordering takeout or grabbing whatever snacks are around, and I’ll keep going past the point where it seems normal. It’s not even like a planned meal. It’s more like I’m standing in the kitchen or sitting there with containers open, just eating because I suddenly feel starving or empty or something.

That’s honestly part of what scared me into coming in. My eating has been all over the place — some days I’m missing meals without meaning to, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks really late. So yeah, for the situation, it does feel like an unusually large amount sometimes.
How often do those late-night eating episodes happen?

It’s kind of inconsistent, which is part of why it’s been hard for me to explain. It’s not like every single night, but it’s happening enough that I noticed a pattern and got worried about it.

Like, some days I’ll go most of the day barely eating — not on purpose, I just get distracted or I forget meals completely — and then later it’s like everything catches up to me after midnight. I’ll end up tearing through takeout or whatever snacks I have around, and it feels out of proportion to the time of night and the situation.

I guess I’d say it happens on and off, but often enough that it doesn’t feel normal for me anymore. That’s honestly one of the things that scared me into coming in, because my eating has just been all over the place.
Over the last 3 months, have those late-night eating episodes happened at least once a week?

Yeah… I think at least once a week is probably fair. It’s hard for me to pin it down exactly because I haven’t been tracking it or anything, but over the last few months, it’s happened enough that it stopped feeling like just a random bad night.

The pattern is more what scares me — some days I’ll forget meals completely, not even on purpose, just get caught up or not think about it, and then other nights after midnight I’m suddenly tearing through takeout and snacks like I’m making up for the whole day. So yeah, I’d say at least weekly, maybe more during some stretches.
Do those late-night eating episodes leave you feeling really upset or distressed afterward?

Yeah… I mean, afterward I do feel pretty upset, mostly because it makes me feel like something is really off with me. It’s not just, “Oh, I had a snack late.” It’s like my eating has been all over the place in a way I don’t really recognize.

Some days I’ll forget meals completely, like I’ll get through the day and realize I barely ate anything, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. And afterward I’m sitting there looking at all the containers or wrappers and thinking, “What am I doing?” That’s the part that scared me into coming in, honestly. It feels out of control and kind of embarrassing, even if I don’t always know how to explain why it happened.
During those late-night eating episodes, do you feel unable to stop eating?

Yeah… during those times it kind of feels like I don’t have the normal “stop” button, if that makes sense. It’s not always that I’m thinking, “I want to keep eating forever,” it’s more like once I start, especially after one of those days where I barely ate or forgot meals completely, I’m suddenly tearing through takeout or snacks after midnight and I’m not really slowing down the way I normally would.

I’ll tell myself, like, “Okay, that’s enough,” and then a few minutes later I’m opening something else or ordering more food or picking at whatever’s left. It feels automatic and out of control in the moment. And then afterward I’m like, why did I do that? That whole back-and-forth is honestly part of what scared me into coming in, because my eating just hasn’t felt normal or steady lately.

doctor.intent: Assess impaired appetite as a depressive neurovegetative symptom to help distinguish major depressive episode from a primary eating disorder or anxiety disorder.
doctor.question: Have you had less appetite lately?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is my eating has been all over the place, like some days I forget meals completely and other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about reduced appetite, which falls under appetite or weight changes.

patient.answer:
Yeah… kind of, but it’s not just less appetite exactly. It’s been really uneven, and honestly that’s part of what scared me into coming in.

Some days I’ll realize it’s like mid-afternoon and I haven’t eaten anything real at all. Not because I’m trying not to eat, I just… forget, or nothing sounds good, or I’m busy and then suddenly hours are gone. And then other nights it swings the other way where it’s after midnight and I’m tearing through takeout or snacks like I’m starving, just eating whatever’s there.

So I don’t know if I’d call it just “less appetite,” because sometimes it’s like I have no appetite, and then later it’s like I’m making up for the whole day all at once. It feels out of control in a weird way.

doctor.intent: Assess psychomotor change to help confirm a major depressive episode and distinguish depression from an eating disorder or nonspecific anxiety presentation.
doctor.question: Lately, have other people noticed that you’re moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: At work I catch myself pacing around my car before appointments and tapping my hands on the steering wheel, but then at home I can sit on the couch and feel like even getting up takes forever.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether others have noticed slowed movement or speech, which directly relates to observable psychomotor slowing.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if people would say “slower,” exactly. I haven’t had someone sit me down and say, like, “You’re moving slow” or anything.

It’s more like I feel kind of all over the place depending on where I am. At work, before appointments, I’ll catch myself pacing around my car in the parking lot instead of just going in. Like I’ll get there early, and instead of sitting still I’m walking around the car, checking my phone, tapping my hands on the steering wheel, almost like I can’t settle my body down. I probably look ridiculous if anyone sees me.

But then when I get home, it’s the opposite. I’ll sit on the couch and it feels like getting up to do one basic thing takes forever. Like I know I should stand up, or go get something, or move to the next room, but my body feels heavy and I just sit there thinking about doing it. So I don’t know if it’s that I’m moving slower all the time, but there are definitely times where I feel slowed down, and other times where I’m kind of restless and can’t stop moving.

doctor.intent: Differentiate major depressive disorder from an anxiety disorder by checking for excessive, hard-to-control worry.
doctor.question: Have you been worrying a lot about different things in a way that feels hard to control?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about excessive, hard-to-control worry across different things, which is more directly an anxiety symptom. The provided symptom profile does not include a specific worry/anxiety item, so I should not force an unrelated bipolar or depressive symptom.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure how to answer that one. I mean, I worry about things, obviously — work stuff, money stuff, whether I’m messing things up — but I don’t know if it’s “a lot” in the way you mean.

It doesn’t feel like I’m sitting there with one worry after another all day that I can’t control, exactly. Sometimes my mind gets stuck on something for a while, but I can usually tell what it’s connected to. Like if something is actually going on, I’ll think about it too much maybe, but I don’t know if I’d call it this constant uncontrollable worrying about everything.

So… I guess I haven’t really noticed that as the main thing. I’d probably need you to explain what you mean a little more.

inference.note: Depressive syndrome remains primary. Generalized anxiety is less supported because he denies pervasive, hard-to-control worry across domains; anxiety/restlessness appears more secondary to mood/work stress. Eating disturbance with irregular restriction/daytime forgetting and late-night loss-of-control eating remains, but without body-image concerns or awakening from sleep, so keep other/unspecified eating disorder diagnoses rather than anorexia/bulimia/night eating syndrome.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the late-night overeating episodes involve objectively large amounts of food, which would help distinguish binge-eating disorder/other specified feeding or eating disorder from appetite disturbance secondary to major depression.
doctor.question: During those late-night episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food for the situation?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is my eating has been all over the place, like some days I forget meals completely and other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about late-night overeating and unusually large food intake, which directly relates to changes in appetite and eating patterns.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I think so. Not every time, but on those nights it feels like a weird amount for that hour, if that makes sense.

Like I’ll have barely eaten during the day — maybe I forgot lunch completely or just had something small — and then after midnight I’m suddenly ordering takeout or grabbing whatever snacks are around, and I’ll keep going past the point where it seems normal. It’s not even like a planned meal. It’s more like I’m standing in the kitchen or sitting there with containers open, just eating because I suddenly feel starving or empty or something.

That’s honestly part of what scared me into coming in. My eating has been all over the place — some days I’m missing meals without meaning to, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks really late. So yeah, for the situation, it does feel like an unusually large amount sometimes.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the binge-like late-night eating is recurrent enough to meet binge-eating disorder criteria rather than being appetite disturbance within a depressive episode or unspecified feeding/eating disorder.
doctor.question: How often do those late-night eating episodes happen?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is my eating has been all over the place, like some days I forget meals completely and other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the frequency of late-night eating episodes, which directly relates to changes in appetite and eating patterns.

patient.answer:
It’s kind of inconsistent, which is part of why it’s been hard for me to explain. It’s not like every single night, but it’s happening enough that I noticed a pattern and got worried about it.

Like, some days I’ll go most of the day barely eating — not on purpose, I just get distracted or I forget meals completely — and then later it’s like everything catches up to me after midnight. I’ll end up tearing through takeout or whatever snacks I have around, and it feels out of proportion to the time of night and the situation.

I guess I’d say it happens on and off, but often enough that it doesn’t feel normal for me anymore. That’s honestly one of the things that scared me into coming in, because my eating has just been all over the place.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the eating episodes meet the frequency threshold for binge-eating disorder rather than being depressive appetite disturbance/other unspecified feeding or eating disorder.
doctor.question: Over the last 3 months, have those late-night eating episodes happened at least once a week?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is my eating has been all over the place, like some days I forget meals completely and other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about the frequency of late-night eating episodes, which falls under changes in appetite and eating pattern.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think at least once a week is probably fair. It’s hard for me to pin it down exactly because I haven’t been tracking it or anything, but over the last few months, it’s happened enough that it stopped feeling like just a random bad night.

The pattern is more what scares me — some days I’ll forget meals completely, not even on purpose, just get caught up or not think about it, and then other nights after midnight I’m suddenly tearing through takeout and snacks like I’m making up for the whole day. So yeah, I’d say at least weekly, maybe more during some stretches.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the binge-eating episodes are associated with marked distress, which would support binge-eating disorder over unspecified feeding/eating disorder or depression-related appetite change.
doctor.question: Do those late-night eating episodes leave you feeling really upset or distressed afterward?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is my eating has been all over the place, like some days I forget meals completely and other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about emotional distress related to the late-night eating episodes, which are part of the patient's appetite and eating-pattern changes.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, afterward I do feel pretty upset, mostly because it makes me feel like something is really off with me. It’s not just, “Oh, I had a snack late.” It’s like my eating has been all over the place in a way I don’t really recognize.

Some days I’ll forget meals completely, like I’ll get through the day and realize I barely ate anything, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. And afterward I’m sitting there looking at all the containers or wrappers and thinking, “What am I doing?” That’s the part that scared me into coming in, honestly. It feels out of control and kind of embarrassing, even if I don’t always know how to explain why it happened.

inference.note: Late-night overeating occurs at least weekly for over 3 months, involves unusually large amounts with loss of control and distress, and is not driven by weight/shape concerns or sleep-related awakenings. This supports a binge-type eating disorder and makes F50.9 less likely/nonspecific.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the binge-eating episodes include objective loss of control, which is the key remaining feature to distinguish binge-eating disorder from appetite disturbance secondary to a major depressive episode.
doctor.question: During those late-night eating episodes, do you feel unable to stop eating?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is my eating has been all over the place, like some days I forget meals completely and other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is directly about loss of control during late-night eating episodes, which falls under the patient's appetite/eating changes.

patient.answer:
Yeah… during those times it kind of feels like I don’t have the normal “stop” button, if that makes sense. It’s not always that I’m thinking, “I want to keep eating forever,” it’s more like once I start, especially after one of those days where I barely ate or forgot meals completely, I’m suddenly tearing through takeout or snacks after midnight and I’m not really slowing down the way I normally would.

I’ll tell myself, like, “Okay, that’s enough,” and then a few minutes later I’m opening something else or ordering more food or picking at whatever’s left. It feels automatic and out of control in the moment. And then afterward I’m like, why did I do that? That whole back-and-forth is honestly part of what scared me into coming in, because my eating just hasn’t felt normal or steady lately.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a depressive episode with at least 4 months of persistent low mood plus marked anhedonia, low energy, insomnia, impaired concentration, guilt, appetite disturbance, and passive death wishes, with clear functional impairment at work and socially. Although there are recurrent distressing late-night overeating episodes with loss of control occurring at least weekly for 3 months, the interview does not establish the full eating-disorder syndrome with sufficient specificity beyond 'other eating disorders'; the overall presentation is better accounted for by a depressive episode in which appetite and eating pattern changes are prominent.
